about: The timeline of TOA: only what has been made public, the latest last in this file. Dates are in Shanghai time (UTC+8). title, text and link are English, each one group marked as the texts of a page are, translated in i18n/<lang>/site/timeline.json.json keyed by the English as a page's catalog is; they hold no double quotes or backslashes. url is a page of the site or an https address. site/build.py renders the timeline page from it, and the latest three on the home page.

events.title: <en>Named TOA</en>
events.text: <en>The format standard for circuit design objects is named TOA, True-OpenAccess, with the GitHub organisation true-openaccess as its home.</en>

events.title: <en>Preview published</en>
events.text: The draft standard 0.1, the reference tool toa and this site are published as a preview, with no release yet. The standard is on the site as web pages, Markdown and PDF.

events.title: <en>Gazettoa online</en>
events.text: <en>Gazettoa, a read-only web browser of TOA libraries, goes online as a preview, with demo libraries.</en>

events.title: <en>Testbenches in the draft standard</en>
events.text: <en>The draft standard says how a testbench measures a circuit: its socket and probes, how a run is assembled, and the targets a circuit can state. The home page shows how to publish the results first and the design later.</en>

events.title: <en>Monte Carlo records</en>
events.text: The draft standard adds evidence records of the kind mc, for Monte Carlo simulations; Gazettoa shows testbenches and these records.

events.title: <en>Timestamps left to their owners</en>
events.text: <en>What a stamps directory holds is up to the owner of the object. The tools page suggests OpenTimestamps, and Gazettoa links to that advice for an object without a proof.</en>
